## Implementation

A layered, hand-written CSV parser (no lookup tables — behavior comes from a character-level state machine):

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/scanner.mbt) | character scanning: unquoted field, quoted field with `""` escapes, terminators (`LF`/`CRLF`/single `CR`) |
| [lexer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/lexer.mbt) | LL(1) token stream `Text · Comma · LineBreak · Eof` from `pos` + `at_field_start` — no lookahead, no buffering |
| [parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/parser.mbt) | fields → records, plus the rectangular-shape check |
| [writer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/writer.mbt) | `print`: quote only what needs quoting, double inner quotes |
| [errors.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/errors.mbt) | `pub suberror ParseError` with offset-bearing messages |
| [csv.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/csv.mbt) | public `parse`/`print` forwarding (declarations stay in `csv_spec.mbt`) |

Semantics follow `specs/csv.md` exactly: empty input → zero records, a trailing terminator adds no record, a blank line is one empty field, a trailing comma adds an empty final field (including at EOF), CRLF is one terminator, CR alone terminates, quotes/`\"` misuse/unterminated quotes/ragged widths all raise. Fields are `StringView` slices of the input, so unicode, emoji and embedded CRLF survive verbatim.

## Implementation

Four focused root-package files, layered so each depends only downwards:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [csv_error.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/csv_error.mbt) | `CsvError` suberror (unterminated quote, quote in unquoted field, text after closing quote, inconsistent field count) + `Show` messages |
| [csv_scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/csv_scanner.mbt) | ASCII character classes and the two field scanners |
| [csv_parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/csv_parser.mbt) | `parse`, the record state machine, rectangularity check |
| [csv_printer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_3/csv_printer.mbt) | `print`, minimal quoting, `""` doubling |

Key design points: one left-to-right pass; a field is copied exactly once as a `StringView` slice, and the second (unescape) pass runs only when a `""` was actually seen. Quote scanning finds the first quote not followed by another, which makes backslash escaping fail naturally (`"a\"b"` closes at the second quote and trips on the stray `b`). Offsets are UTF-16 code units, and since every structural character is ASCII, a scan can never split a surrogate pair. `print` terminates records with CRLF and always ends the last record — `"\r\n"` is the only spelling of a single-empty-record document.

## INI parser implemented

I built a genuine line-oriented INI parser in MoonBit that follows `specs/ini.md` and implements the required root-package API.

### Files

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `ini_scanner.mbt` | physical-line splitting (LF/CRLF), blank/character helpers, trailing-backslash counting |
| `ini_value.mbt` | three value carriers, per-carrier escape decoding, inline comments, continuation joining |
| `ini_parser.mbt` | line classification, section headers, key/value entries, `parse` |
| `ini_printer.mbt` | `print`, double-quote value escaping, safe section headers |
| `ini_rules_test.mbt` | rule-by-rule tests (lines, sections, separators, comments, escapes, continuations, all invalid shapes) |
| `ini_samples_test.mbt` | git-config, systemd and php.ini shaped documents |
| `ini_extra_test.mbt` | 3000-case round-trip and no-panic properties |
| `README.md` | overview, architecture, algorithm details, usage, testing, design rationale |

`ini_spec.mbt`, `ini_qc.mbt`, `specs/`, and `ini_pub_test.mbt` were not modified.

### Behavior highlights

- Line-based classification: blank, full-line comment (`;`/`#`), section header (`[`), or entry — so `key=value [section]` keeps the bracket text.
- Sections: trimmed names, one wrapping quote pair stripped (`["name"]`), quotes elsewhere literal, nested/empty/blank/bracket names rejected, reopened sections accumulate with last-wins.
- Entries: first `=` or `:` wins; keys trimmed, verbatim (backslashes kept), control characters rejected; empty values allowed; duplicate keys last-wins; case-sensitive.
- Values: quoted (`"`/`'`) with quote-specific escape tables, unquoted escapes `\\ \n \r \t`, unknown sequences keep their backslash, inline comments only after whitespace and only on the first segment.
- Continuations: decided on the raw odd/even trailing-backslash run (N=1..4 table verified), joined directly with the pre-marker whitespace kept, continuation lines contribute text only, dangling markers rejected. A file's final line break does **not** count as a line to join, while a real interior blank line does.
- `print` always uses the double-quoted carrier (escaping `\ " LF CR tab`) and adds one outer quote pair only for section names that are themselves quote-wrapped, guaranteeing `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.

## Approach highlights

- **Structural splitting, no heuristics**: the first of `:/?#` decides scheme vs. path, so `a/b:c` is a path while `http://h` is an authority form; `//g` is a network-path reference; `http://` has `host = Some("")`.
- **Whitelist validation per component** (userinfo / reg-name / pchar / query-fragment), percent-encoding checked in the same pass; a single up-front ASCII check rejects non-ASCII, which also keeps code-unit and character indices consistent for `StringView` slicing.
- **Dot-segment removal** keeps the RFC's output buffer as a list of path units, so §5.2.4's "remove the last segment of the output" is a pop and the algorithm is one pass — verified against the complete §5.4.1/§5.4.2 tables (including `http:g` staying `http:g`).
- Scheme lowercased, nothing else normalized; empty (`Some("")`) vs. absent (`None`) preserved, so `Uri::parse(uri.to_string()) == uri`.
